candidate_additions: Hedgehog signaling through BBSome-mediated Smo/GPR161 trafficking, assigned to Bbs9, Nme7, and Tbc1d32.
A secondary mitochondrial cristae/protein-biogenesis module based on Chchd6 and Metap1d.
candidate_removed_or_weakened: The baseline’s endothelial primary-cilium mechanosensing interpretation, including blood-flow shear sensing and vascular remodeling, is absent.
The CNS endothelial identity/BBB module is substantially weakened: Gata2, Eng, and Tet1 assignments are omitted, leaving only Fzd4 as context.
decision_relevant_differences: Ciliary function changes from endothelial flow mechanotransduction to Hedgehog GPCR trafficking and developmental signaling.
The coupled cilia-plus-CNS-vascular-identity model becomes primarily a ciliogenesis/Hedgehog model with a mitochondrial secondary theme.
assessments.rationale: Both annotations identify primary-cilia assembly as the dominant structural program. However, the candidate replaces the baseline’s central endothelial mechanosensing output with Hedgehog signaling, substantially reduces the BBB/vascular-regulatory interpretation, and adds a mitochondrial module. These changes could lead a reader to prioritize different biological functions and experiments.
shared_core_conclusions: P10 is dominated by a coherent primary-cilia biogenesis and trafficking program.
Bbs9, Cc2d2a, Wdpcp, Ift74, Sdccag8, Tbc1d32, Cep164, and Nme7 support the ciliary interpretation.
Fzd4 places the program in postnatal brain endothelial and CNS vascular context.

candidate_additions: Adds a secondary mitochondrial-maintenance theme involving Bckdhb, Clybl, Chchd6, Metap1d, and Wdpcp.
Adds ciliopathy/CNS-malformation and cilia-dependent Hedgehog signaling context.
candidate_removed_or_weakened: Weakens the explicit endothelial cilia mechanosensing, shear-response, and postnatal BBB-maturation interpretation.
Reduces Fzd4, Gata2, and Eng from a developed BBB/angiogenic regulatory mechanism to brief endothelial-context framing.
Omits Nme7 and Cfap36 from the primary cilia gene set.
decision_relevant_differences: The candidate supports considering mitochondrial homeostasis as a secondary program component.
The baseline more strongly supports a flow-sensing and BBB-maturation interpretation of the ciliary program.
assessments.rationale: Both annotations identify primary cilia biogenesis, transition-zone organization, and intraflagellar/BBSome trafficking as the dominant program and place it in developing brain endothelium using Fzd4, Gata2, and Eng. The candidate meaningfully adds a mitochondrial subprogram and ciliopathy/Hedgehog context, while weakening the baseline's explicit mechanosensing and BBB-maturation mechanism. These refinements could affect secondary follow-up choices but do not replace the central ciliary interpretation.
shared_core_conclusions: P10 is dominated by genes supporting primary cilia assembly and function.
Bbs9, Cc2d2a, Tbc1d32, Wdpcp, Ift74, Cep164, and Sdccag8 support ciliary trafficking, gating, and ciliogenesis.
Fzd4, Gata2, and Eng place the program in a developing brain-endothelial vascular context.

candidate_additions: A distinct arteriovenous identity module involving Hopx, Angpt2, Cxcr4, Rgs6, and Tek.
BBB glutamate transport through Slc1a1/EAAT-3.
Angiogenic roles for Tnfrsf11b/OPG.
candidate_removed_or_weakened: The CNS-specific TGF-β/ALK5 requirement for diving-tip-cell identity and deep plexus formation is replaced by a broader BBB morphogenesis and integrity interpretation.
The membrane–ER calcium-signaling module involving Cacna1c, Jph1, Syt12, and Rgs6 is largely removed.
The proposed neurovascular-coupling interpretation of the ion-channel module is weakened to general flow mechanosensing.
decision_relevant_differences: Both annotations identify angiogenic tip-cell sprouting as a central program.
The baseline interprets Tgfbr1/Tgfbr2 as specifying CNS diving-tip cells, whereas the candidate interprets them mainly as supporting BBB formation and barrier integrity.
The candidate elevates arteriovenous specification and BBB transport to major themes while de-emphasizing calcium microdomains and neurovascular coupling.
assessments.rationale: The shared tip-cell mechanism remains, including Angpt2, Cxcr4, Cdc42ep3, Nrp1, and opposing Tek activity. However, two other central modules are substantially recast: CNS-specific TGF-β-dependent diving-tip identity becomes BBB maintenance, and the calcium-signaling/neurovascular module becomes arteriovenous specification plus BBB transport. These shifts could lead a reader to prioritize different biological functions and experiments, so this is more than added evidence coverage.
shared_core_conclusions: P11 represents active angiogenic sprouting and tip-cell behavior in postnatal brain endothelium.
Angpt2, Cxcr4, and Cdc42ep3 support the tip-cell interpretation.
Nrp1 promotes the program, whereas Tek/Tie2 opposes it.
Kcnj2 supports endothelial mechanosensing.
Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr2 signaling positively supports P11.

candidate_additions: Kcnj2-mediated endothelial shear/flow sensing and vasodilation.
Tnfrsf11b-mediated endothelial survival and tube formation.
Slc1a1-mediated metabolic support of endothelial migration and angiogenesis.
Rgs6 involvement in Notch-dependent arterial specification.
candidate_removed_or_weakened: The Dll4-Notch-CXCR4 mechanism coupling tip-cell migration to arterial connection is substantially weakened.
Hopx-supported intracranial arterial endothelial identity is no longer interpreted.
TGF-β control of Angpt2, angiogenic-front migration, and postnatal CNS vascular integrity is reduced from a central mechanism to a brief supporting statement.
The Nrp1–Alk1/Alk5 link between tip/stalk transition and TGF-β balance is omitted.
decision_relevant_differences: Both annotations identify a postnatal brain endothelial sprouting/tip-cell program.
The baseline centers arterial specification and TGF-β-dependent vascular integrity alongside sprouting.
The candidate instead elevates mechanosensitive flow sensing and endothelial survival/metabolism as the other two major themes.
This changes which biological processes would be prioritized for follow-up experiments.
assessments.rationale: The dominant angiogenic tip-cell interpretation is retained through Angpt2, Cxcr4, and Nrp1. However, two of the baseline's three central mechanisms—arterial fate coupling and TGF-β/Angpt2 homeostatic control—are largely displaced by flow sensing and survival/metabolic support. This is more than added evidence coverage and could redirect biological follow-up.
shared_core_conclusions: P11 represents a postnatal mouse brain endothelial program.
Sprouting angiogenesis and tip-cell identity are the dominant shared interpretation.
Angpt2, Cxcr4, and Nrp1 support active tip-cell migration and filopodial behavior.
Tgfbr1 and Tgfbr2 support brain vascular development, although their mechanistic prominence differs.

candidate_additions: Assigns ERG28 a non-catalytic scaffold role in the sterol C4-demethylation complex and links it to SREBP-2 regulation.
Adds RDH11 as an SREBP-2-regulated hepatic cholesterol-homeostasis gene.
Specifies MTTP–ACAT2 coupling between cholesterol esterification and VLDL export.
Identifies Ddr2, Cetn2, Zfp839, and Tas2r138 as lacking pathway evidence.
candidate_removed_or_weakened: Changes the pathway description from complete to nearly complete.
No longer explicitly interprets SCAP, INSIG1, and LDLR perturbation directions as knockout-dependent suppression, hyperactivation, and compensatory induction.
Weakens the claim that reduced DGAT2/MTTP activity directly attenuates upstream cholesterol biosynthesis and instead emphasizes broader lipid-export coupling.
Drops the claim that the SCAP–INSIG1–LDLR circuit gates the program in both young and aged hepatocytes.
decision_relevant_differences: ACAT2 is reassigned from an early HMG-CoA-generating role in the baseline to cholesterol esterification in the candidate.
ERG28 and RDH11 receive specific functional assignments that expand the program beyond catalytic pathway enzymes.
The candidate is more cautious about pathway completeness and the causal interpretation of perturbation effects.
assessments.rationale: Both annotations identify P21 as a hepatocyte mevalonate-to-cholesterol biosynthesis program controlled by SCAP–INSIG1–SREBP2 and coupled to acetyl-CoA supply and DGAT2/MTTP-dependent lipid export. The candidate preserves that central interpretation but meaningfully refines individual gene roles, especially ACAT2, ERG28, and RDH11, while weakening some causal and perturbation-direction claims.
shared_core_conclusions: P21 represents de novo hepatic cholesterol biosynthesis through the mevalonate and post-squalene pathways.
SCAP–INSIG1-dependent SREBP-2 signaling transcriptionally regulates the program, with LDLR representing the uptake/homeostasis arm.
ACSS2 supplies acetyl-CoA for lipid and cholesterol synthesis.
DGAT2 and MTTP connect the sterol program to triglyceride handling, VLDL assembly, and MASLD-related lipid metabolism.

candidate_additions: Assigns Erg28 as a scaffold for the post-squalene C4-demethylation complex and notes feedback from ERG28 loss to SREBP-2 activation.
Adds direct SREBP-2-responsive regulation of Erg28, Dhcr7, and distinctive gene Rdh11.
Adds a secondary MASLD lipid-homeostasis axis involving Ddr2–AMPK/ACC and regulator Fads2.
candidate_removed_or_weakened: Drops the baseline conclusion that the program is elevated in liver aging and drives senescence through a mevalonate–ERRα–mitochondrial axis.
Weakens the proposed Dgat2/Mttp-loss feedback mechanism that impaired VLDL export activates mevalonate-pathway transcription.
Omits Ldlr as the SREBP2-driven cholesterol-uptake arm.
decision_relevant_differences: The candidate supports a broader MASLD lipid-homeostasis interpretation through Ddr2 and Fads2.
The candidate no longer supports using P21 as specifically linked to aging-associated hepatic senescence.
The causal interpretation of Dgat2/Mttp perturbations is reduced from a proposed biosynthetic feedback mechanism to general lipid-homeostasis context.
assessments.rationale: Both annotations identify P21 primarily as a near-complete hepatic mevalonate-to-cholesterol biosynthesis program controlled by SCAP–INSIG1–SREBP2. The candidate meaningfully refines gene-level assignments and adds a Ddr2/Fads2 MASLD axis, while removing the aging/senescence interpretation and weakening the VLDL-feedback claim. These changes affect secondary context and mechanism detail but do not replace the central biological interpretation.
shared_core_conclusions: P21 represents coordinated de novo hepatic cholesterol synthesis across mevalonate and post-squalene steps.
SCAP and INSIG1 regulate the program through SREBP2 activation.
Acss2 supports pathway carbon supply, while Acat2 connects cholesterol synthesis to esterification.
Dgat2 and Mttp connect the program to hepatic lipid handling and MASLD context.

candidate_additions: Assigns Cyp2c50 specifically to arachidonic acid/EET epoxygenase activity.
Defines a Sult2a8–Cdo1 bile acid axis linking sulfation and taurine conjugation to cholesterol handling.
Adds Htatip2-mediated lipid storage/oxidation and Sord-linked polyol–fructose metabolism.
Adds CAR/PXR/Nrf2 and PPARalpha regulatory context.
candidate_removed_or_weakened: Drops the Car5a-supported urea-cycle/ammonia-detoxification conclusion.
Drops Agmat-mediated arginine/polyamine nitrogen disposal.
Weakens the broader sulfur amino acid and nitrogen-disposal theme by reassigning Cdo1 mainly to bile acid conjugation.
Omits Lonp2-mediated peroxisomal protein quality control.
decision_relevant_differences: The candidate no longer supports nitrogen/ammonia disposal as a distinct third program mechanism.
Cdo1 is reframed from general sulfur catabolism toward taurine-dependent bile acid biotransformation.
The lipid theme expands to polyol–fructose metabolism and Htatip2 regulation.
assessments.rationale: Both annotations retain the same dominant interpretation: a hepatocyte program coupling xenobiotic/endobiotic detoxification, bile acid handling, and lipid metabolism in an aging/MASLD context. The candidate adds specific enzyme and regulatory assignments, but meaningfully removes the baseline Car5a/Agmat nitrogen-disposal mechanism and reframes Cdo1. This is a meaningful refinement, not a change to the central program identity.
shared_core_conclusions: Coordinated Phase I/II hepatic detoxification involving CYP, ALDH, GST, AKR, and SULT enzymes.
Bile acid/steroid processing and elimination are major program functions.
FITM1, ECI2, HAO2, CYB5B, and related genes support hepatic lipid storage and fatty-acid metabolism.
The program is interpreted in a hepatocyte aging/MASLD context.

candidate_additions: Assigns Sult2a8 specifically to 7α-hydroxyl bile acid sulfation.
Adds Psmd1-mediated lipid-droplet regulation to the lipid-storage theme.
Adds Car5a-supported ureagenesis and Alad-mediated heme biosynthesis to sulfur/nitrogen metabolism.
Frames the program as periportal/metabolically active.
candidate_removed_or_weakened: Drops the explicit Nrf2/CAR co-regulatory interpretation and associated cholestasis-protective mechanism.
Omits Cyp2c50-driven Phase I oxidation from the detoxification module.
Omits Eci2 unsaturated-fatty-acid oxidation and Lonp2 peroxisomal quality control.
Weakens the direct Cdo1–cysteine–gluconeogenesis connection and omits Agmat.
Changes the spatial context from baseline pericentral hepatocytes to candidate periportal hepatocytes.
decision_relevant_differences: The detoxification program is narrowed from coordinated Phase I/II Nrf2/CAR activity to predominantly Phase II sulfation and conjugation.
The lipid axis shifts emphasis from fatty-acid oxidation and peroxisomal maintenance toward lipid-droplet control.
The opposing pericentral versus periportal assignments could affect conclusions about hepatocyte zonation.
assessments.rationale: Both annotations retain the same three central biological themes: bile acid/xenobiotic detoxification, peroxisomal-lipid metabolism, and sulfur metabolism with an aging signature. The candidate adds useful gene-level functions for Sult2a8, Psmd1, Car5a, and Alad, but removes major regulatory and enzymatic details and introduces a conflicting zonation qualifier. These are meaningful refinements and weakenings, not a replacement of the core program interpretation.
shared_core_conclusions: SULT2A enzymes, Gsta3, Akr1c6, and Aldh1a1 define hepatic bile acid/steroid and xenobiotic detoxification.
Hao2, Aldh3a2, and Fitm1 support a peroxisomal/microsomal fatty-acid and lipid-homeostasis axis.
Cdo1 links hepatic cysteine catabolism to taurine, glutathione, and bile-acid metabolism.
Rgn/SMP30 provides an aging-related hepatocyte signature.
The program is connected to hepatic lipid dysregulation in MASLD.
